summary:
The product design is sound and matches the tree. The three routes compose calls that already exist: GET / uses Library.Latest, GET /reports/{slug} uses PublishedBySlug, and GET /raw/{slug} uses OpenRaw(slug, true) followed by serveRaw(…, "no-cache"). The two-state error mapping is right, and so is moving TestStoreErrorDeniesAdmin from 200 to 503 with its anonymity checks kept. html/template escapes the sign-in next value, and the link no-go is settled as an author contract. I read router.go, raw.go, home.go, admin.go, harness_test.go, signin_test.go, admin_test.go, layout.html, home.html, reports.go, the fitness rules and the rule runner. Every code claim I checked holds. No existing test breaks except the one the design names.

The fixes are all minor, in the browser assay and the new tripwires:
- **Unenforced background colour.** The assay's "the site chrome shows neither signal colour" precondition holds today only because someone remembers it. SC-010 adds likes to this exact layout, and a CSS `red` is pure #ff0000, which the assay would read as "a script ran".
- **The second must-verify is not checked per run.** It is checked only by a different Edge process (W4), not within W1's own run.
- **The https well has no beacon log.** The zero-beacon assertion covers server P only. W1s runs on a second harness whose log is never named.
- **Two tripwires miss common spellings (CC-001):**
  - the template rule stays quiet on an iframe with no sandbox attribute at all, and on object, embed and frame tags;
  - the draft rule misses the gofmt multi-line OpenRaw(…, false,) call;
  - the byte-path rule misses http.FileServer(http.Dir(…)) and os.DirFS.
- **Contradictory renderReader contract.** It both receives and "builds" readerData.

On the two must-verify preconditions:
- **If Edge's command-line screenshot leaves out out-of-process frame pixels**, or virtual time does not wait for them, the frames never paint. W4 cannot turn red and the run fails loudly, so it never passes falsely. The cost is building the DevTools fallback, which is the ~200-line piece the selection cut.
- **If a capture comes too early**, W4 catches that only in its own process. Reordering the reagent makes "green" itself prove that the parser got past the script, so the check holds in every well.

Searches found nothing against the headless claims:
- Chromium's headless command handler exists (https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/main/components/headless/command_handler/headless_command_handler.cc).
- One project reports that --virtual-time-budget forces a --headless=new --screenshot capture to finish (https://github.com/convenientlymike/svgsafe/commit/b1ca16ec8b9122064e31e14b07cff9f32fe88972).

Whether that capture includes out-of-process frame pixels can only be settled by running Shot against W4 on this machine's Edge.

findings.claim: The assay's validity depends on an invariant that nothing enforces: no element of the real reader chrome may render pure #00ff00 or #ff0000. The design records this precondition as 'holds' only because today's site.css uses neither colour; the 'Reader styles' component itself says 'The site CSS must not use pure #00ff00 or #ff0000'. W1, W1s and W2 require exactly red = 0 over the WHOLE image. SC-010 and SC-011 will add the like count and comments to this same shared layout, and a heart styled `color: red` is #ff0000. The assay would then report 'a script ran under the shipped sandbox', a false alarm on the slice's central risk, and the obvious 'fix' for it is to loosen the threshold. No well measures the site chrome on its own, so the cause cannot be told apart from a real script run.
findings.evidence: Design: Reader styles ('The site CSS must not use pure #00ff00 or #ff0000, because the browser assay relies on that'). cross_domain_transfer invariant 'Neither assay colour appears in the instrument's own background. holds: site.css uses neither colour'. Verdicts 'W1, W1s, W2, W3: green ≥ 40,000 px and red = 0'. A grep of internal/server for #0f0, #00ff00, #f00, #ff0000, red, lime and rgb( found nothing today. The slice brief says SC-010 and SC-011 add the like count and comments to this shared layout.
findings.fix: Add an instrument-blank well that shoots the real reader chrome with nothing framed (P's GET / before the reagent is uploaded, i.e. the 'No reports yet' state). Require green = 0 and red = 0 in it, and fail as 'invalid run: the site chrome contains a signal colour'. Alternatively, add a fitness rule over internal/server/static/** and internal/**/templates/** that forbids #0f0, #00ff00, #f00, #ff0000, red and lime.

findings.claim: The second must-verify precondition (the capture happens after the inline script had its chance to run) is checked only across runs. The design says 'an early capture leaves the positive control not red, and the run fails', but W4 is a separate Edge process with its own timing. Nothing in W1's own run shows that the capture came after the parser reached the <script>. In the reagent as specified, the green <style> comes first and the script and onerror image come after it. A W1 frame painted green before the parser reached the script would read as 'rendered, no script'. The false pass is narrow: it needs the sandbox and CSP to fail AND the capture to be early. But this is exactly the precondition the design imported without proof.
findings.evidence: Design, Browser isolation assay: 'an inline
findings.fix: Put the green <style> element at the end of the reagent's body, after the script and the onerror image, and have the script and handler set inline styles (element.style outranks the stylesheet). Green in any well then means the parser got past the script, so precondition 2 holds within every well rather than only by the cross-process control.

findings.claim: The case for the https well says 'The hband server must log no /beacon request', but W1s runs on 'a second harness over https', and the design wraps only 'Server P' in a request log. The zero-beacon assertion therefore never covers the https well. Nothing requires the log to contain the wells' own traffic either, so a wrapper installed on the wrong handler would pass 'no /beacon/' vacuously. Each harness builds its own httptest server and handler, so wrapping one does not cover the other.
findings.evidence: Design: 'Server P is the harness, wrapped in a request log' … 'W1s: the same reagent on a second harness over https' … 'P's log holds no /beacon/ request at all'. Case 'read a report in a real browser': '…over http and over https… The hband server must log no /beacon request.'
findings.fix: Wrap both harnesses (P over http and the TLS harness) in request logs, and assert zero /beacon/ requests on each. Make each log non-vacuous by also requiring GET /raw/probe in it for every well that targets that server (W1, W2 and W5 on P; W1s on the TLS harness).

findings.claim: The template tripwire forbids only bad sandbox TOKENS. It stays quiet on the most direct breach of the constraint: an <iframe> to /raw/<slug> with NO sandbox attribute at all. It is also quiet on <object data=…>, <embed src=…> and <frame>. TestReportPage pins the attribute on report.html alone. A later template (SC-010/SC-011 on this layout, or a show-all page) could frame a report unsandboxed and only the rawCSP header would remain, while the rule and the corpus pass. RE2 has no lookahead, so 'an iframe lacking sandbox' cannot be written as one regex. Forbidding the tag outside an allowlist of files can.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml, rule 'no site template frames a report with scripts or the site origin, or inlines it'. The design's corpus plan lists fire rows only for allow-scripts, allow-same-origin and srcdoc. The rules are evaluated per whole file (internal/fitnessrules/rules_test.go:156-163).
findings.fix: Add a token rule: `(?i)<(iframe|frame|object|embed)\b` must not match in internal/**/templates/**, with except_files internal/server/templates/report.html and internal/server/templates/admin_report.html. Add corpus rows: fire on `<iframe src="/raw/{{.Slug}}">` in a new template, quiet on report.html.

findings.claim:
The draft and byte-path tripwires miss ordinary Go spellings (CC-001):
- The draft rule `\.OpenRaw\(.*,\s*false\s*\)` is matched against the whole file with `.` not crossing newlines. The gofmt multi-line call `OpenRaw(\n\tr.Context(), slug, false,\n)`, which ends in a trailing comma, is quiet. So is a publishedOnly flag held in a variable, which bounded_by names.
- The byte-path rule `\bhttp\.Serve(Content|File|FileFS)\(` is quiet on `http.FileServer(http.Dir(dataDir))` and `http.FileServerFS(os.DirFS(...))`. Those are the likeliest accidental way to expose <data>/reports/*.html under the site CSP. The design's bounded_by names only io.Copy, and its corpus deliberately keeps FileServerFS quiet.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml rules 'report bytes are written only by serveRaw' (line 155) and 'only the gated admin reaches drafts' (line 175). The runner applies each pattern to the whole file text (internal/fitnessrules/rules_test.go:162). The only FileServerFS in the tree serves the embedded static FS (router.go:62), never http.Dir or os.DirFS.
findings.fix: Use the token form (lesson #931): forbid `\.OpenRaw\(` everywhere except internal/server/raw.go, internal/server/admin.go and internal/reports/**, and let TestHiddenReportsAreIndistinguishable pin readRaw's `true`. Add `\bhttp\.(Dir|FileServer)\(` and `\bos\.DirFS\(` to the byte-path rule's must_not_match; router.go's `http.FileServerFS(staticSub)` stays quiet. Add fire rows for the multi-line OpenRaw call and for http.FileServer(http.Dir(dir)).

findings.claim: The renderReader contract contradicts itself. Its signature is renderReader(w, r, status, readerData), which means the caller supplies the data, yet the same component 'builds readerData{pageData{Title, SignedIn, Viewer, Next}, …}'. It also says Title must be rep.Title+" - hband" and Next must come from the STORED slug, 'never from the request'. If the two callers (home and readReport) build readerData, then Title, Next and Viewer are composed at two call sites. The 'same layout' property (C2) and the next-from-stored-slug rule then hold only as long as both callers remember them, and SC-010 and SC-011 will extend this same function.
findings.evidence: Design, Reader handlers: 'renderReader(w, r, status, readerData): the only path either page takes; builds readerData{pageData{Title, SignedIn, Viewer, Next}, Report, HasReport, Unavailable}; Title is rep.Title+" - hband" … Next is … "/reports/"+rep.Slug from the STORED slug'. Contract 'renderReader(w, r, status, readerData)'.
findings.fix: Fix the signature as renderReader(w, r, status, rep reports.Report, state) with state one of found, empty or unavailable. Inside it, derive Title, Next ("/" or "/reports/"+rep.Slug), SignedIn and Viewer (from auth.ViewerFrom(r.Context())), so neither handler can compose them differently.

findings.claim: Shot promises that 'a leftover [profile] is logged, not fatal', and that a timeout kills only the process Shot started. The natural implementation, --user-data-dir=t.TempDir(), contradicts the first promise: testing's TempDir cleanup reports a failed RemoveAll through t.Errorf. After a timeout kill, Edge children that still hold the profile (renderers, the crashpad handler) would turn a lingering lock into a failed test. Separately, if stdout or stderr is captured into a buffer, cmd.Wait waits for every process holding the pipe, and without cmd.WaitDelay that wait is unbounded after the kill.
findings.evidence: Design, Headless browser helper: '--user-data-dir=<fresh temp>' … 'on timeout kills only the process it started, never by name; removes the temp profile with bounded retries, and a leftover is logged, not fatal'. The frame-render spike had to kill 10 leftover Edge processes holding its scratch profile.
findings.fix: Specify os.MkdirTemp for the profile, with the helper's own bounded-retry removal in t.Cleanup that only logs a leftover (never t.TempDir). Set cmd.WaitDelay, for example to 5 s, so Wait returns after the kill even if a child still holds an inherited pipe.

findings.claim: Making /raw/{slug} public lets any anonymous client hold a report's file open: a slow or repeated GET, or many Range requests, each keep the *os.File open for the length of ServeContent. On a Windows host the existing replace path then cannot set the old file aside, and the owner gets the 409 'being read right now' refusal. Until now only the owner's own preview could do that. The design does not mention this interaction. Production is a Linux Docker container (Q-004), so this affects only Windows runs such as this dev machine, which is why it is filed as extra.
findings.evidence: TestReplaceWhileThePreviewIsOpen pins that a replace is refused on Windows while a reader holds the file. readRaw keeps OpenRaw's *os.File open through serveRaw's http.ServeContent (raw.go:26-37). adminSave maps reports.ErrBusy to 409 (admin.go:92-93).

quote.text: // On Windows a replace cannot set aside a file somebody is reading: the owner

findings.fix: Record it as a known Windows-host limit in the readRaw comment. Optionally add one TestPublicRawAfterReplace sub-case, Windows-only, that holds GET /raw open during a replace and expects the 409 refusal while the old bytes stay intact, so the behaviour is pinned rather than discovered.

dimensions_checked.result: m1: the assay has no in-run blank for the real site chrome. The 'no signal colour in the background' precondition is remembered rather than enforced, and SC-010 and SC-011 add UI to this exact layout.

None material. The https well W1s cites lesson #933, which is about a cookie reaching the frame; /raw reads no identity, so that cookie question does not arise. The well still exercises https frame-ancestors matching for one more Shot, which is cheap. Six wells, three tripwires and twelve HTTP tests fit a high-risk isolation slice. The DevTools client was rightly deferred behind the Shot signature.

m6: the renderReader signature both receives and 'builds' readerData, so the Title and Next derivations could end up per caller. The GET /, /reports/{slug} and /raw/{slug} contracts are otherwise complete for status, headers, HEAD and 304.

m7: the headless profile cleanup and Wait behaviour after a kill. Checked the reader error mapping against TestStoreErrorDeniesAdmin (admin_test.go:326-329): moving it from 200 to 503 keeps its anonymity checks valid, because Identify leaves a store-down viewer anonymous. readRaw returns 500 when a file is missing, matching adminRaw (admin.go:129-133). A template error stays a 500 via a.render.

None. The switch from beacon to colour assay follows the build-check measurement that img-src data: suppresses the beacon. The spike's link no-go is resolved by an explicit author contract plus the upload-form hint, without changing either CSP. The routes match the approved e001 excerpts recorded by the spike acceptance-tests-match-reader-routes.

m2: the capture-timing must-verify is checked only by a different process; reordering the reagent makes it hold per well. m3: zero beacons are unasserted on the https harness, and no log is required to contain the wells' own traffic.

If must-verify 1 fails (the command-line capture leaves out frame pixels), W1 and W4 never colour. The run fails as invalid, never a false pass, and the DevTools fallback must be built.

Settling must-verify 1 needs one run of Shot on W4 against this machine's Edge 158.

verdicts.checked: I re-read the prescribed wells, run conditions and outside claims against raw.go:15-19 (rawCSP: default-src 'none', img-src data:) and against the build-check measurement: under rawCSP no plain-img beacon was requested, while the img-src 'self' control fetched its img. I traced W3: Q serves the reagent with no CSP, under a sandbox attribute without allow-scripts, and the frame has a real src URL, so it inherits no policy from its parent. The frame's origin is opaque, but sandbox does not restrict image loads, so resolves to Q and is fetched. I traced W4: allow-scripts with no CSP, so the inline script's /beacon/script?w=W4 reaches Q. A cross-origin fetch from an opaque origin still sends the GET. I traced W5: it frames P, so any beacon from it would go to P, not Q, and the well tags keep W3 and W4 apart in Q's log. Changing ?w= changes only a query string, so W3 is still 'the same bytes' for the attribute-alone purpose.
verdicts.why: The reframing is correct. P's zero-beacon count measures rawCSP's request blocking, not script execution. A script running under rawCSP would have its beacon blocked either way, so only the red pixel count can say whether a script ran. W3's /beacon/img is the right control for that blocking: the same tag in the same reagent, differing only in the absence of rawCSP. Tagging each copy with its well removes the W3/W4 merge. I found no well, start state or spelling where the three conditions pass vacuously.

verdicts.checked:
I compared the design's report.html branches: with HasReport, an h1, the 'Published' date, the permalink and the .report-frame iframe with a 1px #8884 border; when empty, only

No reports yet.

. I re-read the slice brief: 'The like count and comments beneath the report are added to this shared layout by SC-010 and SC-011'. A grep of internal/server for signal colours found none today.
verdicts.instead: Shoot the blank in the found-state layout. Upload a second published report 'blank' through the same POST /admin/reports: a neutral body (for example a #808080 background), no script, no signal colour. Shoot P's /reports/blank, anonymous like W1, and require green = 0 and red = 0, failing as 'invalid run: the site chrome contains a signal colour'. Because it uses /reports/blank rather than /, it does not depend on Latest or on upload order. The empty-state shot can stay as a second blank.

verdicts.checked: I traced the reordered reagent: script, then the onerror image, then the green
verdicts.why: The per-well timing proof covers the inline script only. The parser can reach the trailing green <style> and paint green before the onerror event is dispatched. If the capture lands in that gap, W1 reads 'rendered, no handler ran' whether or not the handler would have run. That is exactly what precondition 2 left open, now only for the second probe. W4 cannot cover it: in W4 the inline script turns the page red first, so W4 never shows that the onerror channel alone fires within the budget. Separately, a builder who writes the green rule with !important silently defeats the red repaint in every well.
verdicts.instead: State that the per-well guarantee holds for the inline <script>. For the onerror probe, add a positive-control well W4b: the reagent with the inline script removed, so only the onerror image is left, under sandbox="allow-scripts" with no CSP. Require red ≥ 40,000 px, which shows the handler fires and repaints within the capture budget. Also require that the reagent's green rule carries no !important, and that both repaints use element.style.

verdicts.checked: I read harness_test.go:102-114: each harness has its own httptest server, whose handler reads h.handler under h.mu. A log wrapper can therefore be set by swapping h.handler to wrap(New(...)) outside the security chain. I listed which wells target which server: W1, W2 and W5 on P, W1s on the TLS harness. Only W2's and W5's /raw URLs can carry a query tag, because W1's iframe src comes from report.html ('/raw/{{.Report.Slug}}').
verdicts.why: The logs are cumulative across wells. 'Each log must hold GET /raw/probe for every well aimed at that server' is satisfied on P by a single /raw/probe from any one of W1, W2 or W5. If W1's frame never requested /raw/probe (it rendered something else, or the wrapper was on the wrong handler for that request), the check still passes on W2's hit, and the vacuity the fix exists to remove returns per well. Also, nothing requires P's and the TLS harness's wrapper to be the same code as Q's. If they differ, Q's /beacon/img hit (M-add-1) does not show that P's logger records beacon paths at all.
verdicts.instead: Run the Shots in sequence. Before each Shot, record the length of every log, and judge each well on that Shot's own entries: W1, W2 and W5 must each add GET /raw/probe to P, W1s must add it to the TLS log, and no Shot may add a /beacon/ entry to P or TLS. Install the wrapper by setting h.handler under h.mu, outside New's chain, so it sees mux 404s too. Use one wrapper type for P, TLS and Q, so Q's tagged hits show that the same logger records /beacon/ paths.

verdicts.checked: I grepped internal/ for <(iframe|frame|object|embed|fencedframe|portal): the only hit outside tests is admin_report.html:22, so the rule would be quiet on the tree. `<frame\b` does not match <frameset. I globbed internal/server/static/**: only site.css today. router.go:24-25 embeds the whole of static, and router.go:62 serves it under siteCSP via http.FileServerFS. rules_test.go:234-237: a corpus row with no path defaults to internal/server/x.go.
verdicts.why: The files glob internal/**/templates/** leaves out internal/server/static/**. Anything placed in static/ is embedded and served at /static/... under siteCSP, whose frame-src 'self' allows framing /raw/<slug>. A static .html page can therefore frame a report with no sandbox attribute while the rule and the corpus pass. That is the very bypass m4 was raised to close. Also, the prescribed fire row `<iframe src="/raw/{{.Slug}}">` written without a path is evaluated at internal/server/x.go. There the templates glob does not apply, so the row fails TestRuleSpellingsCorpus, or a builder 'fixes' it by weakening the row. <fencedframe> is not listed either.
verdicts.instead: Give the rule files 'internal/**', with except_files '**/*.go', internal/server/templates/report.html and internal/server/templates/admin_report.html. The tree walker already skips testdata, and the only non-Go file today is site.css, so it covers templates/ and static/ and stays quiet now. Add fencedframe to the alternation: <(iframe|frame|fencedframe|object|embed)\b. Give both corpus rows explicit paths: fire at internal/server/templates/new.html and at internal/server/static/x.html, quiet at internal/server/templates/report.html.

verdicts.checked: I read .taad/fitness.yaml:172-185. The draft rule is one rule, three patterns (.OpenRaw(…false), .BySlug(, .ListAll() and one except_files list. rules_test.go:138-147 applies except_files to the whole rule. I grepped the tree for \.OpenRaw\b, \.BySlug\b, \.ListAll\b, os.DirFS, http.Dir( and http.FileServer(. Outside tests the only hits are admin.go:73, 105 and 124 and upload.go:317. There is no DirFS, Dir or FileServer anywhere. `\bhttp\.(Dir|FileServer)\(` does not match router.go:62's http.FileServerFS(.
verdicts.why:
Three paths are left open.
- **raw.go escapes the draft checks.** readRaw in raw.go must call OpenRaw, so the token form needs raw.go excepted. Done the obvious way, by editing the existing rule, that adds raw.go to an except list it shares with .BySlug( and .ListAll(. The public byte-path file, the one place a draft leak matters most, then escapes all three draft checks.
- **Method values pass.** `\.OpenRaw\(` misses a method value: `open := a.reports.OpenRaw; open(ctx, slug, false)`. The same holds for BySlug and ListAll. CC-001 names this accessor variant explicitly.
- **cmd/ is never checked.** The byte-path rule's files are internal/**/*.go, so cmd/hband/*.go, where the data dir is configured and the handler is composed, could mount http.FileServer(http.Dir(dataDir)) unchecked.
verdicts.instead: Make the OpenRaw token a separate rule, 'only raw.go and admin.go open report files', with pattern `\.OpenRaw\b` and except_files internal/server/raw.go, internal/server/admin.go, internal/reports/** and **/*_test.go. Leave the existing BySlug/ListAll rule's except list as it is (admin.go, internal/reports/**, tests), and change its patterns to `\.BySlug\b` and `\.ListAll\b`. Widen the byte-path rule's files to '**/*.go', keeping internal/server/raw.go and **/*_test.go excepted and adding internal/testutil/**. It stays quiet on today's tree. Add fire rows for the gofmt multi-line OpenRaw call, for a method value `f := a.reports.OpenRaw` at internal/server/reader.go, and for http.FileServer(http.Dir(dir)) at cmd/hband/main.go.

verdicts.checked: I traced the prescribed signature renderReader(w, r, status, rep, state), with state found, empty or unavailable, through the design's two callers and its Next rule: Next is "/" for the home page and "/reports/"+rep.Slug for a report page, from the stored slug, never from the request. TestReaderPagesShareOneLayout expects the anonymous bodies to differ only by next decoding to / and to /reports/<slug>. home.go:19 confirms auth.ViewerFrom(r.Context()) returns (Viewer, bool).

prescribed.summary:
Of the seven prescriptions, one holds (M-add-1) and six have holes. All the holes are minor, and each can be fixed inside the same file the prescription already touches.

- **m1:** the blank well uses the 'No reports yet' state, and that state renders nothing in the report branch: no h1, no date, no permalink, no frame border. SC-010 and SC-011's like count and comments go beneath the report, so the case that motivated the finding is exactly what the blank never shoots.
- **m2:** moving the green style to the end proves timing for the inline `<script>`. The onerror handler is asynchronous, so green can paint before it fires.
- **m3:** the request logs are cumulative, so 'GET /raw/probe for every well' passes on a single hit unless each Shot's own slice of the log is checked.
- **m4:** the files glob covers templates/ only. internal/server/static/ is embedded and served under the site policy, so a static HTML page can frame a report unsandboxed. Also, a corpus row with no path defaults to x.go, which the templates glob never applies to.
- **m5:** if raw.go is added to the existing draft rule's except_files, raw.go, the public byte-path file, also escapes the .BySlug( and .ListAll( checks. `\.OpenRaw\(` misses a method value. The byte-path rule never looks at cmd/.
- **m6:** the prescribed renderReader(w, r, status, rep, state) cannot tell the home page from a report page when both show a report. So Next ('/' versus '/reports/<slug>') cannot be derived without reading the request, which the design forbids. Status and state are also two parameters a caller can pass out of step.
